main_text.p: dæt[?], cum de pecuniis fermo eft, Centum five quinquies viginti; cum de pecore, sexies viginti denotare, nemo eft apud nos qui non intelligat. In posteriore item exemplo, illa vox Bushell[?] cum apud Meridionales Anglos ex usu communi modium Latinorum unicum significet, apud Septentrionales binos modios[?]: usus locorum ambiguitatem ejus vocis ita definiret, ut utrovis loco contractus fieret, de fenfu tamen verborum inter bonæ fidei viros nulla poffet-effe diffen-fio. Exemplum tertii: Caii agrum quendam é mult s[?] unum fundo suo vicinum Titius emere cupiens, de pretio cum eo aliquoties ante collocutus, ubi eum die quodam convenit, Dabin' mihi, inquit, agrum tuum eo quo dixi pretio? Dabo. Jura mihi te daturum. Juro. Etsi de eo agro qui Titii fundo vicinus eft peculiaris nulla facta fit mentio: certum eft tamen ex antegreffis fermonibus eundem illum agrum peculiarem intelligi. Et iftiusmodi quidem Juramentum obligat[?] jurantem ad præstandum bona fide ic[?] quod promisit eo fenfu, in quem manifeftum eft, fi abeffet utrinq; omnis dolus malus, utrumque contrahentium confenfiffe. Fidem violaret Caius, fi Titio aliun

page.notes: Page begins mid-word ("dæt", probably the end of a word from the previous page); the first paragraph is therefore a continuation. The Anglo-Saxon/black-letter word "Bushell" in the first line of the middle paragraph is set in a Gothic-type form and is uncertain. "modios" is partly obscured. "mult s" appears as printed (a letter seems missing, perhaps "multis"); left as printed. "ic" at the end of a line may be "id" partly cut off by the clipped margin. "obligat" has its final letters obscured. The right margin is clipped by the scan edge; the fragments there cannot be read and are not transcribed as notes. The catchword "aliquen" is cut off as printed. No heading or signature is visible.
